Substantival adjective; the supplied them that is its own rendering, headed on the lexeme-bearing mourn.
Nomen rectum of the construct chain; the ASV recasts of Zion as in Zion, so the connective stays with Zion.

Attributive rendering former (rule 28).

First of two absolute occurrences of דּוֹר in the repetition figure, which the ASV renders once; tail-to-tail puts the rendering on the last (rule 22). Placing of generations here and marking the second occurrence unrepresented remains defensible.
The ASV writes no and inside דּוֹר וָדוֹר.
Rendered occurrence of the repeated noun; it carries the nomen rectum's of (rule 19) and the many that English supplies for the repetition figure.

Verbless clause: the supplied copula shall be belongs to the predicate noun it licenses (rule 20).

One Hebrew substantive rendered by the ASV's hyphenated vine-dressers, tokenized in two; rule 31's subtraction puts the head on vine, which carries the denominative lexeme כֶּרֶם, rather than on the supplied agentive dressers, which alone names no vine-tender.

Gapped תַּחַת: the supplied *instead of* joins the noun it governs (rule 34), never `added`.
The *in* supplied for the adverbial accusative belongs to the noun licensing it (rule 33).
לָכֵן fuses into one English word (rule 30); headed on the adverb כֵּן as the lexeme carrier rather than the preposition, though the briefing's gloss places *therefore* on the preposition.
